title: Shadow Load & Chaos Eval Playbook for Quant-Aware Rollouts
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview:

This playbook describes the end-to-end process for running controlled shadow-load and chaos evaluations when rolling out quantized model artifacts across Redwood’s hosted, dedicated, and private deployment modes. The procedure is intended for ML engineers, SREs, release engineers, and applied ML owners responsible for model promotion and post-launch quality guardrails.

Goals:

- Validate functional parity and degradation boundaries for quantized model artifacts under representative and stress traffic.
- Exercise fallback and routing policies (e.g., model-variant fallback, region fallback, capacity-tier fallback) under load and partial failure.
- Measure end-to-end telemetry coverage required to detect token-level and prompt-level quality regressions introduced by quantization.
- Produce deterministic, repeatable judgement artifacts for promotion decisions and postmortem investigations.

Scope and When to Use:

Use this playbook when:
- Promoting a new quantized build (all precisions: int8, mixed FP16/INT8, hybrid) to shadow or canary.
- Introducing new KV cache or prefix caching changes that interact with quant artifacts.
- Deploying major changes to the serving runtime or kernel selection logic that could alter execution paths under quantized code paths.
- Performing cross-environment verification (hosted -> dedicated -> private).

Not in scope: training-time checks, offline-only unit tests.

Key Roles and Ownership:

- Model Owner (Primary): defines acceptance criteria, prompt set anchors, and quality thresholds.
- Release Engineer: orchestrates shadow traffic, configures sequencer and chaos injections, and runs the scheduling pipeline.
- SRE / Platform: validates routing, capacity shaping, and metrics ingestion.
- Eval/QA Engineer: runs the annotation job, computes drift/quality metrics, and signs off on gating results.

Success Metrics (examples):

- Functional Delta: composite response similarity score >= 0.92 vs baseline (defined by owner).
- Latency SLO: p95 latency overhead of quantized variant vs baseline model <= 25 ms for production slices.
- Token-Error Budget: token-level degradation rate <= 0.5% on high-sensitivity slices.
- Failure Recovery: automated fallback to baseline model within 5s of observed error budget breach.
- Telemetry Coverage: at least 95% of shadowed requests should include trace id, prompt anchor id, KV-cache-key, and model-variant tag.

Test Scenarios and Templates:

1) Baseline Parity Run (Low load):
- Purpose: Validate deterministic functional parity on stable prompt anchors.
- Traffic: 2x representative prompt per anchor, sequenced single-threaded.
- Observables: deterministic hashes, embedding cosine similarity, response-length distribution, and top-level functioncall fidelity.

2) Production Shadow (Representative load):
- Purpose: Surface distributional regressions when mixing real production traffic with shadow routing.
- Traffic: Live sampled traffic at 10–30% shadow rate; preserve header propagation and user-affinity tokens.
- Observables: A/B logging of prompt context, latency histograms, sampling of populated KV-cache vs misses.

3) Stress Burst (Load shock):
- Purpose: Validate batching, kv-cache eviction patterns, and runtime kernel fallbacks under microbursts.
- Traffic: Synthetic bursts at 3–5x baseline QPS for 60–120s windows scheduled across hours to validate autoscaler behavior.
- Observables: queue latencies, batch size distributions, tail latency percentiles, and missed functioncalls.

4) Cache-Degradation Mode:
- Purpose: Measure quality impact of intentionally reduced cache hit-rate (simulates cold starts).
- Traffic: Replayed sequences with randomized prefix truncation to reduce KV cache effectiveness by target factor (e.g., -40% hits).
- Observables: delta on token spend, latency, response divergence.

5) Chaos Scenario Matrix (Partial failure modes):
- Purpose: Exercise graceful degradation and fallback routing.
- Faults to inject: kernel OOM on a subset of GPU workers, transient RPC errors on seq-batcher, delayed KV-store responses, and corrupted quant tables (manifest-level error).
- Observables: error spikes, increased fallback invocations, rollback triggers, and alert noise level.

Telemetry & Signal Requirements:

Minimum required signals for every shadowed request (collect at ingress and runtime):
- trace_id (string), prompt_anchor_id (string), model_variant (string), quant_profile (string), kv_cache_hit (boolean), batch_id (string), kernel_path (string), latency_ms (numeric), token_count (numeric), response_hash (string), annotator_sample_flag (boolean).

Instrumenting synthetic probes and anchors:
- Use the shadow-sequencer service with these conventions: prefix anchor keys with SHADOW-<owner>-<run-id>.
- Set annotator_sample_flag=true for 1% of requests to route to the annotation queue for human review.
- Export telemetry to both APM (traces) and our Eval Data Lake with consistent partition keys for reproducibility.

Annotation and Aggregate Metrics:_guidelines:

- Sampling strategy: stratified by slice importance (high-sensitivity > medium > low). Target annotation budget: 500 labels per high-sensitivity slice per rollout.
- Aggregates to compute: response-stability-index (RSI), semantic-similarity (embedding cos), BLEU-like edit distance for structured outputs, and functioncall fidelity.
- Decision thresholds: if RSI drop > 0.06 on any high-sensitivity slice or semantic-similarity drop > 0.08 -> fail gating unless mitigation plan provided.

Gating & Promotion Criteria:

Promotion to canary/dedicated/private requires:
- All smoke scenarios pass with no critical regressions.
- Automated metrics within defined thresholds for 24h representative shadowing.
- No >1 critical incident attributed to quant path (critical = data loss, P95 latency > 2x SLO, or silent failure causing incorrect structured responses).

Gating outputs (artifact checklist):
- Telemetry snapshot (1h and 24h).
- Annotated sample set with annotator consensus.
- Deterministic diff report: token	non-deterministic regions	likely-cause.
- Rollout plan with capacity knobs and emergency rollback steps.

Runbook: Step-by-step Playbook for a rollout window (condensed):

1) Pre-flight (T-48 to T-1):
  a) Owner declares acceptance criteria and slice list.
  b) Release engineer provisions shadow run id and config in shadow-sequencer.
  c) SRE validates capacity reservation and autoscaler thresholds.
  d) Telemetry team validates ingestion routing and partitioning.
  e) Kick off a quick parity run (Baseline Parity) and store baseline artifacts.

2) Shadow Run (T0 -> T+24):
  a) Start representative shadow at configured rate (default 10%).
  b) Enable annotator sampling and delayed sampling for tails.
  c) Run scheduled Stress Bursts and Cache-Degradation scenarios at pre-announced times.
  d) Monitor dashboards: model-quality, latency, batcher health, and fallback counters.
  e) If any mid-severity signal breaches threshold, pause bursts and increase annotator sampling.

3) Chaos Window (T+6h typical):
  a) With SRE & Release Engineer present, run one or more fault injections from the matrix.
  b) Observe automated fallback behavior: verify requests routed to baseline variant, and that fallback counts and latencies are within expected.
  c) If silent degradation is observed (quality drift without obvious errors), mark for regression triage and halt promotion.

4) Post-run (T+24 -> T+72):
  a) Eval Engineers produce an automated judgment report and tag any offending slices.
  b) Annotators label flagged items and provide root-cause hypotheses.
  c) If metrics are within thresholds, owner signs off to proceed to canary; else, owner documents mitigation steps and re-run plan.

Rollback & Emergency Steps:

- If critical failure observed: trigger emergency rollback via inference-router policy: set model-routing to baseline and disable quantized variant. Expected rollback latency target: < 60s to be effective across regions.
- Post-rollback: collect full trace exports for the last 15 minutes and open regression triage ticket with priority P0.

Configuration Examples (YAML used by shadow-sequencer):

# Example shadow run configuration
shadow_run_id: "SHADOW-asha-2026-02"
owner: "asha.patel@redwood.ai"
shadow_rate: 0.15
model_variant: "m-proto-7b-quant-int8-v2"
baseline_variant: "m-proto-7b-fp16-v1"
stress_burst_windows:
  - start: "2026-02-19T10:00:00Z"
    duration_seconds: 90
    multiplier: 4
chaos_injections:
  - type: "rpc_delay"
    target: "seq-batcher:region-a"
    percent: 5
    delay_ms: 250
annotator_sampling: 0.01
kv_cache_hit_target: 0.65
telemetry_tags:
  - "shadow"
  - "quant-int8-v2"

(above YAML is a config example to paste into shadow-sequencer UI; adapt fields for private deployments where network namespaces differ).

Triage flow for detected regressions:

1) Detection: Eval alert fires (owner & eval team notified).
2) Quick triage (15–30m): reproduce on parity runner with same seed and request anchor.
3) Attribution (1–4h): determine if regression is model-level (quant artifacts), runtime kernel, or infra. Use kernel_path, batch traces, and quant_profile to isolate.
4) Remediation: if kernel/runtime, patch and re-run shadow job; if model quant artifact, consider re-quantizing with fallback to mixed-precision.

Notes & Practical Tips:

- Always pin baseline_variant to an immutable artifact ID to avoid moving baselines.
- Use trace sampling keys to ensure that the same request id is available across both baseline and quant logs for deterministic diffs.
- For private/on-prem customers, ensure the Eval Data Lake signer role is available; otherwise replicate minimal telemetry via secure S3 bucket.

Appendix: Recommended Dashboards and Alerts (minimum):

- Quality Dashboard: RSI by slice, semantic-similarity histograms, annotator backlog.
- Runtime Dashboard: p50/p95/p99 latencies by model_variant, batch sizes, kernel_path distribution.
- Chaos Dashboard: injected fault counters, fallback counts, rollback triggers.
- Alerts: RSI_drop_high_sensitivity (severity P1), fallback_rate_high (P2), p95_latency_multiplier > 2x (P0).

Related artifacts to attach to promotion ticket:

- 1h and 24h telemetry snapshots (parquet), annotated sample set (CSV + JSONL), deterministic diff report (HTML), shadow run config (YAML), chaos injection log (JSON).

End of playbook.
